title: Reviving Willie Cook from an overdose in Canada
summary: He and Procope rescued Willie Cook after an overdose, walking him with coffee; Cook later thanked him, and Tizol deplores the drug problems.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: No. But I got a good story about Cook, the little trumpet player.

That was when we were in Canada. Some woman called and said that [Willie] (Jimmy) Cook was in there on the floor, and she was scared, because I think he knocked himself out, you know? With one of those shots. You see, so she asked if one of us could come and get him and do something about him, because she was by herself and she couldn't do nothing.

So me and Procope, we got in a cab and we went down to this house, where he was out there, and we hit him; you know, we gave him some coffee and we just did everything to wake him up, you know? But he had shot himself over, you know, because he did that many times; he used to do it all the time because a lot of things, in theatres, he used to go in the men's room and one time I saw blood in the seat of the toilet, and that's where he used to do it. He shot himself.
And this time, he overdosed, yeah. But
I got him over and we took him back to our hotel. But the woman was scared to death because she thought he was dead or something, you know? We took an awful chance to go over there and pick him up.
Well, how did you get him concious again?

We walked him, you know? They say when a person gets that way, you take him and walk him; walk him around, and once in awhile, you hit him in the side and wake him up and slap him, you know? They don't feel it, but they start getting up. And coffee, too, black coffee especially. That's good for it.
How long did it take to bring him around?
Oh, not too long, but we scuffled with him quite awhile. He always thanked me for that, you see, he used to say, 'I want to thank you for saving my life'.
Yeah. I understand he is behaving himself now.
I don't know what he is doing now.
I understand he lives in Texas and has a business.
He was a pretty good trumpet player, you know? And for some reason or another, I used to like him, you know? But I wouldn't stand for the foolishness that he

used to do in the band. And I gave him money; I used to give him money, like if we went to play someplace, I don't know where it is, and the band would be given dinner, and he wouldn't eat nothing. So I would beg him, I would say, 'Man, come on -- get something to eat.' But I would give him $5 and tell him to get whatever he wanted; maybe he didn't like what they had. I would give him $5 for him to get something to eat.
Oh, we had some awful men in that band.
Yeah, it was a problem, I know, many times.
Oh, how Duke could stand all that stuff, I don't understand. That's what I fought with him about all the time.
